known.title: case --loop with a recorded candidate contract overlay passes null prompts to writeRuns, so a candidate loop cannot be built
known.summary: After `agents --candidate-contract-overlay` records `candidateContractDiff`, armSpec gives each candidate code arm a `contractDiff` (prepare.mjs:929-930), so `prompts` is null (line 940). The loop branch (lines 943-946) does not handle the overlay and pushes `{ dir, meta, prompts }` with that null, and writeRuns iterates `for (const { reviewer, text } of prompts)` (line 744), which throws a TypeError; the catch removes the new case folder. So `case --loop --arms C1` or `C3` cannot prepare any review. Plan decision 8 (plan line 47) wants each run of a candidate code arm to get the contract copy and a prompt that names it, and the later rounds of a loop would review without that copy. The fix is a clear refusal of `case --loop` for a candidate arm with the overlay, or loop prompts that keep the overlay, with a test.

known.title: The new --candidate-contract-overlay flag is tested only through prepareAgents, not through the command line
known.summary: The overlay test (review-benchmark.test.mjs:6067-6101) calls `prepare.prepareAgents(agentOptions, repo)` with `'candidate-contract-overlay': true` (line 6073) and bypasses the CLI option parser. If the registration `'candidate-contract-overlay': { type: 'boolean' }` (prepare.mjs:1740) is removed, the test stays green, while the documented command `prepare.mjs agents --candidate-contract-overlay` fails with an unknown-option error. A CLI-level check of the flag is missing.

known.title: The plan-reviewer wrapper accepts a Files cell that covers the reviewer folders from above or with a glob, so a changed local reviewer can set its own review
known.summary: Without an installed plugin, the plan-reviewer wrapper (.codex/agents/plan-reviewer.toml:12-16) and its template (codex-agent-templates.md:26-30) use the project-local reviewer 'only when no Files cell of the plan export names a path in' the reviewer agent and skill folders. A Files cell such as `plugins/plan-lifecycle/` or a glob such as `plugins/plan-lifecycle/**` covers these folders without naming a path inside them, so the check passes and a plan that changes the local reviewer is reviewed by that changed copy. Plan decision 7 wants that no plan or diff can change the instructions of its own review. The check must also refuse an ancestor folder and a covering glob, and treat a cell that it cannot rule out as covering.

known.title: The blocked answer of both Codex wrappers has no review heading, so the plan helper ignores it and keeps an earlier pass
known.summary: When the installed plugin is missing and the fallback is refused, both wrappers (code-reviewer.toml:16-18, plan-reviewer.toml:16-18) and both templates (codex-agent-templates.md:30-32, 62-64) tell the reviewer to return 'the line `Code-review: blocked` (or `Plan-review: blocked`) and one line that names the missing installed plan-lifecycle plugin'. This answer has no review heading. parseReviewComment (plan.mjs:794-799) returns undefined when the first line does not match REVIEW_HEADING (`/^(?:#+\s*)?(plan|code) review/i`, plan.mjs:771), and `Code-review` has a hyphen, so a posted blocked answer is not a review, and reviewVerdicts (plan.mjs:818) keeps any earlier pass. The wrapper must return a block with the heading of the dispatched mode, a blank line, and the blocked verdict line.

known.title: The results log still says that the code decision uses the panel cases, against the pooled five-case decision
known.summary: results.md:913 says 'Thus the code decision uses the panel cases.' The repaired Decision section (results.md:943-945) now decides C1 on all five code cases, pooled, with the delta case, as plan decision 5 fixes. The two texts give different deciding sets, so a reader does not know which set decided. The sentence must say that the single-case delta table is a diagnostic and that the code decision pools the five code cases.
